name: Dolores 'Lola' Fitzgerald

five_sec.what_is_it: HelloFresh. The food boxes my sister sent me. With some kind of prize game on top.
five_sec.who_for: People who want boxes of food shipped.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Open A Box To Reveal Your Offer.' That's how they get you. My sister got charged after she cancelled one of these.
five_sec.next_step: Find the little 'Continue Without Offer' and go.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Green boxes with the name on them. I've had one on my porch.

full_page.what_stopped_me: It's a food box, and the small print says auto-renewing. I can't read that tiny gray writing without my glasses anyway. Cheese, cream, butter in near every supper on there.
full_page.whats_missing: A price I can see. Anything plain the little one would eat. Dairy-free.

HF.quote: Pick a box for a prize, then a paragraph of tiny print. Ayuh, I know how this ends. With a charge.

five_sec.what_is_it: A recipe app. Recipes and grocery lists on your phone.
five_sec.trust_why: It says no card, and has stars. But it says 'Free Trial,' and a trial is a trial.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Picture of a lady writing a list.

full_page.what_stopped_me: It's $5.95 a month after two weeks, and I'd have to find all the recipes myself. That's the part I can't do. A big '50% OFF' clock counting down at the bottom made me nervous.
full_page.whats_missing: Suppers picked for me. Anything about milk allergies.

PTE.quote: It says nothing to cancel, which is kind. But I'd still have to find the suppers myself, and that's my whole trouble.

five_sec.what_is_it: Something that texts the family supper ideas and makes the grocery list.
five_sec.who_for: Families with kids that have phones.
five_sec.trust_why: It says plain as day 'We don't deliver food' and 'no card needed.' Those are my two questions answered.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The dark green words, 'We don't deliver food. We plan your week and send your grocery list.'

full_page.what_stopped_me: There's a free one and a $4.99 one, and the free 14 days. That sounds like a subscription even if it says no card. The setting for each child's allergies is on the $4.99 plan. And the sample week has 'Creamy Tomato Pasta,' which is just what Lily can't have. I don't see Hannaford named.
full_page.whats_missing: Something showing I can mark Lily dairy-free for nothing. A phone number or some way to reach a person on the front page; I only saw an email on the other page. Bigger writing.

DD.quote: Sarah says she's a parent and it's free with no card. That's kind. But the sample's got 'Creamy Tomato Pasta,' and that's Lily sick.

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal plans of some sort. 'Less Stress, More Dinners.'
five_sec.trust_why: It doesn't say what it is or what it costs. Just a video.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: A phone with food all around it. Might be a box, might not.

full_page.what_stopped_me: A box popped up for my email, 'Try Free for 14 Days' everywhere, no price. That's a trial and they'll want a card.
full_page.whats_missing: A dairy-free plan. They've got fifteen and none says dairy-free. A price.

EM.quote: Fifteen plans, keto and paleo and all that, and not one says dairy-free. And no price. No thank you.

five_sec.what_is_it: A phone app. Something about dinner and a 'mental load.'
five_sec.trust_why: The big orange button is a letter from somebody's CEO. I don't know what I'd be signing up for.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Pictures of food on a phone. Could be anything.

full_page.what_stopped_me: It says AI writes the recipes. I don't trust a computer with Lily's milk allergy. And the price is in the app, or $25 a month on another page.
full_page.whats_missing: Anything about allergies. A plain price.

OL.quote: A computer writing the recipe for a child with a milk allergy? I don't think so.

dd_offer.why: It says no card, and nothing to cancel. But then there's $4.99 and $39 a year right beside it, and 'Add a card now.' I'd want my daughter to read it with me.
dd_offer.expect_day_15: I think the texting part stops and the rest stays free, since they never had my card. But I'd still be watching my bank.

head_to_head.reason: It's the only one that told me straight off it isn't a box of food and won't take my card.

HF.reason: HelloFresh is a food box that renews itself.

PTE.reason: Plan to Eat costs after two weeks and doesn't pick suppers for you.

EM.reason: eMeals is a trial with no price and no dairy-free plan.

OL.reason: Ollie has a computer writing recipes; DinnerDrop has a real mother behind it.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page, Sarah's 'Why I built DinnerDrop' letter: put a way to reach her right there (the email that's only on the pricing page, or a number to text), and say in plain words whether I can keep a whole week dairy-free on the free plan. A real person I could ask is what would get me past the worry.
